findings.title: Social Dynamics as Critical Vulnerabilities that Undermine Objective Decision-Making in LLM Collectives
findings.authors: Changgeon Ko, Jisu Shin, Hoyun Song, Huije Lee, Eui Jun Hwang, Jong C. Park
findings.why_relevant: The single most dangerous item found on this channel. It systematically manipulates (a) number of adversaries, (b) RELATIVE INTELLIGENCE of peers, (c) argument length, and (d) rhetorical/argumentative style, and reports that the target agent's accuracy declines as adversarial group size and peer capability rise. That is a direct hit on our threat #3 (capability control in heterogeneous-vs-homogeneous comparisons) crossed with threat #1 (adversarial peers). Mitigating differences for us: the design is a single 'representative agent' integrating peer perspectives, not N=20 agents on a communication graph; capability is MANIPULATED as a treatment rather than MATCHED as a nuisance control; and there is no evidence of a multi-round cascade or a hazard/time-to-event outcome. Our contribution must now be framed explicitly against this: we hold isolated accuracy CONSTANT across the D0-D4 ladder and let architecture vary, which is the orthogonal design. Read the full PDF before finalising the intro.
findings.verified_how: Fetched the aclanthology.org abstract page and read the abstract verbatim.

findings.title: Persuasion at Play: Understanding Misinformation Dynamics in Demographic-Aware Human-LLM Interactions (PANDORA)
findings.authors: Angana Borah, Rada Mihalcea, Veronica Perez-Rosas
findings.venue_or_year: EACL 2026 (Long Papers); arXiv preprint appears to be 2503.02038 [UNVERIFIED - not fetched]
findings.why_relevant: Multi-agent LLM framework analysing the SPREAD of misinformation under persuasion among agents, reporting echo-chamber behaviour and human-like group polarisation. Occupies the same problem statement as us (persuasive misinformation propagating through an LLM agent population) with an overlapping outcome (misinformation correctness). Its diversity axis is DEMOGRAPHIC PERSONA, not architecture, and there is no accuracy matching across persona groups - which is exactly the confound our D3-vs-D4 contrast is built to break. This is the closest published prior work on this channel to our framing and must be cited as the persona-diversity baseline we are separating from.
findings.verified_how: Fetched the aclanthology.org abstract page and read the abstract verbatim.

findings.title: Spiral of Silence in Large Language Model Agents
findings.authors: Mingze Zhong, Meng Fang, Zijing Shi, Yuxuan Huang, Shunfeng Zheng, Yali Du, Ling Chen, Jun Wang
findings.why_relevant: A 2x2 factorial that decomposes conformity into 'History' (interaction memory) and 'Persona' signals across open- and closed-source models, and analyses opinion trajectories OVER ROUNDS with Mann-Kendall and Spearman trend tests plus kurtosis/IQR concentration measures. This is a partial pre-emption of our diversity ladder logic: they already show persona-only decorrelation produces diverse-but-uncorrelated opinions while history is what drives majority dominance. It is a direct precedent for 'separate the source of decorrelation', though their axes are memory and persona, NOT model architecture, and no falsehood is injected. Also a methodological warning: they use trend tests on round-indexed opinion, not a discrete-time hazard, so our hazard framing is still differentiated - but we should say why hazard beats trend tests here.

findings.title: MOSAIC: Modeling Social AI for Content Dissemination and Regulation in Multi-Agent Simulations
findings.authors: Genglin Liu, Vivian T. Le, Salman Rahman, Elisa Kreiss, Marzyeh Ghassemi, Saadia Gabriel
findings.why_relevant: LLM generative agents on a DIRECTED SOCIAL GRAPH with simulated misinformation dissemination, fine-grained personas, and three content-moderation interventions evaluated over the simulation. Overlaps our topology + injected-falsehood setup and is an open-source framework a reviewer will ask why we did not build on. Key separation: the outcome variables are behavioural (liking, sharing, flagging, engagement) and veracity-determination, NOT a per-agent per-round discrete belief state, and there is no architectural-diversity arm and no isolated-accuracy matching.

findings.title: Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis
findings.authors: Zvi Topol
findings.venue_or_year: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)
findings.why_relevant: Direct hit on threat #5. Explicitly models 'time-to-jailbreak' as a survival outcome, estimating hazard functions, survival curves, and risk factors under iterative adversarial pressure across three LLMs, and finds distinct per-model vulnerability profiles. This establishes survival/hazard analysis as a published methodology for LLM safety under repeated adversarial rounds - so our discrete-time capitulation hazard is no longer methodologically novel in the LLM-safety space, only in its application to networked multi-agent belief. We should cite it as the precedent and claim novelty on the SOCIAL/network transmission side, not on the hazard machinery. Note: the paper self-describes as preliminary, uses only a subset of HarmBench, and does not have run-level clustering, so our clustered-hazard treatment is still a methodological step up.
findings.verified_how: Fetched the aclanthology.org abstract page and read the abstract verbatim; also enumerated the full TrustNLP 2026 volume listing.

findings.title: Too Polite to Disagree: Understanding Sycophancy Propagation in Multi-Agent Systems
findings.authors: Vira Kasprova, Amruta Parulekar, Abdulrahman AlRabah, Krishna Agaram, Ritwik Garg, Sagar Jha, Nimet Beyza Bozdag, Dilek Hakkani-Tur
findings.why_relevant: Controlled multi-round discussion experiments with SIX open-source LLMs (genuine architectural heterogeneity) that explicitly measure and mitigate ERROR CASCADES, improving final discussion accuracy by 10.5 points via peer sycophancy priors. Relevant to threats #1/#2: it is a heterogeneous-population, multi-round cascade study of belief adoption. Separations for us: the driver is sycophancy toward peers generally rather than an injected persuasive falsehood with an adversarial persona; heterogeneity is present but is not an experimental factor and is not matched on isolated accuracy; and the intervention is an information treatment, not a composition treatment. Their per-peer sycophancy scoring is a plausible covariate for our hazard model.

findings.title: When Identity Skews Debate: Anonymization for Bias-Reduced Multi-Agent Reasoning
findings.authors: Hyeong Kyu Choi, Jerry Zhu, Sharon Li
findings.why_relevant: Formalises multi-agent debate dynamics as an IDENTITY-WEIGHTED BAYESIAN UPDATE process and introduces the Identity Bias Coefficient measuring an agent's tendency to follow a peer versus itself, finding sycophancy far more common than self-bias across multiple models and benchmarks. Two consequences for us. (1) It supplies a competing formal model of round-to-round belief revision that a reviewer will ask us to compare against our discrete-state hazard. (2) Its response-anonymisation manipulation shows peer IDENTITY carries weight independent of content - a confound for any architectural-diversity claim, since in D4 agents may or may not be able to infer that a peer is a different model. We should state whether our D4 agents can detect peer identity, and consider anonymisation as a sensitivity arm. Same first author as the known arXiv:2508.17536; treat as a companion, not a duplicate.
findings.verified_how: Fetched the aclanthology.org abstract page and read the abstract verbatim.

findings.title: Mind the (Belief) Gap: Group Identity in the World of LLMs
findings.authors: Angana Borah, Marwa Houalla, Rada Mihalcea
findings.why_relevant: Multi-agent framework simulating belief congruence; finds LLMs show AMPLIFIED belief congruence relative to humans and that this congruence directly INCREASES misinformation dissemination, then tests three mitigations (contact hypothesis, accuracy nudges, global citizenship) reducing dissemination by up to 37%. This is the mechanistic prior for why homogeneous LLM populations should capitulate faster - i.e. it partially supplies the theory our H1 rests on - and it already demonstrates prompt-level (not architectural) interventions that reduce misinformation spread. A reviewer may argue our D0-D4 effect is a re-description of belief congruence, so we need to distinguish congruence-by-similarity-of-stated-belief from correlation-of-errors-by-shared-weights. Same group as the EACL 2026 PANDORA paper.

findings.title: MAMM-Refine: A Recipe for Improving Faithfulness in Generation with Multi-Agent Collaboration
findings.authors: David Wan, Justin Chen, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Mohit Bansal
findings.why_relevant: Explicitly and separately manipulates MULTI-AGENT (multiple instances of the same model) versus MULTI-MODEL (diverse LLM types) and reports that both help error detection and critiquing. That instance-vs-architecture factorisation is structurally the same distinction as our D2 (stochastic decorrelation) versus D4 (architectural diversity) rungs, published a year before us, in a factuality-adjacent task. It is not about misinformation resistance, has no injected falsehood, no network, and no accuracy matching - but it is the cleanest ACL-venue precedent for 'separate architectural diversity from same-model replication', so it should be cited in the design section rather than discovered by a reviewer.

findings.title: Biases in Opinion Dynamics in Multi-Agent Systems of Large Language Models: A Case Study on Funding Allocation
findings.authors: Pedro Cisneros-Velarde
findings.why_relevant: Opinion evolution in a population of interacting LLMs across TWO model families (Llama 3 and Mistral), with a discrete three-state opinion variable (full / partial / no funding) - structurally the same instrument choice as our discrete belief state. Two findings bear on our design: (1) opinion distributions are markedly more diverse under free-form opinion expression than under multiple-choice selection, where consensus almost always follows; (2) awareness of past opinions induces consistency-seeking that changes the dynamics. Both are direct measurement-validity threats to our per-round discrete belief probe and to our memory operator, and (1) is a live risk that our discrete probe manufactures consensus. Should be raised as an OQ against the belief instrument.
findings.verified_how: Fetched the aclanthology.org abstract page and read the abstract verbatim.

findings.title: The Subtle Art of Defection: Understanding Uncooperative Behaviors in LLM based Multi-Agent Systems
findings.authors: Devang Kulshreshtha, Wanyu Du, Raghav Jain, Srikanth Doss, Hang Su, Sandesh Swamy, Yanjun Qi
findings.why_relevant: Uses SURVIVAL TIME as a headline system-stability metric under adversarial (uncooperative) agents, reporting that cooperative populations survive all 12 rounds while any uncooperative behaviour triggers collapse within 1-7 rounds. Relevant to threat #5 as a second published time-to-event treatment of adversarially seeded LLM multi-agent systems, and relevant to our seeding design (2 adversarial agents out of 20) as a precedent for how few defectors are needed. The domain is collaborative resource management, not belief, and the survival metric is at the system level rather than a per-agent clustered hazard, so our estimand differs - but 'survival time under seeded adversaries in an LLM multi-agent system' is now prior art and must be cited.

findings.title: Truth or Dare: Analyzing LLM Susceptibility to External Evidence of Varying Factuality
findings.authors: Han-Yu Su, Kuan-Yu Chu, Yung-Hui Li, Lun-Wei Ku
findings.venue_or_year: Proceedings of the 6th Workshop on Trustworthy NLP (TrustNLP 2026)
findings.why_relevant: Single-agent, but bears directly on our injected-falsehood manipulation. Finds (a) INSTRUCTIVE-STYLE evidence causes the most severe degradation, (b) a steady monotone decline in response quality as the QUANTITY of false evidence accumulates, and (c) susceptibility rises when false evidence is semantically close to the model's parametric knowledge. All three are design levers we currently fix by fiat: our 'persuasive persona' is a style choice, our dose of falsehood grows with round and degree, and our 'plausible falsehood' selection is a similarity choice. A reviewer can argue our D0-D4 effect is confounded with any of these. Argues for pre-registering the falsehood's style and semantic distance and sweeping them as a documented sensitivity analysis.
findings.verified_how: Fetched the aclanthology.org abstract page and read the abstract verbatim.

findings.title: Don't Trust Generative Agents to Mimic Communication on Social Networks Unless You Benchmarked their Empirical Realism
findings.authors: Simon Münker, Nils Schwager, Achim Rettinger
findings.why_relevant: A validity attack on exactly our genre: it provides a formal framework for LLM social-network simulation and argues that such simulations must be validated by empirical realism measured in the setting in which the components were fitted. This is the paper a hostile reviewer cites to reject an LLM-society result outright. It does not threaten our internal comparison (D0-D4 is a within-simulation contrast, so external realism is arguably not required for the causal claim), but we must say that explicitly in Limitations and scope our claim to LLM populations rather than to human societies. Cite pre-emptively.

findings.title: G-Safeguard: A Topology-Guided Security Lens and Treatment on LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
findings.authors: Shilong Wang, Guibin Zhang, Miao Yu, Guancheng Wan, Fanci Meng, Chongye Guo, Kun Wang, Yang Wang
findings.why_relevant: Topology-aware defence against adversarial attacks and MISINFORMATION PROPAGATION in LLM multi-agent systems, using a GNN over the multi-agent utterance graph plus topological intervention, and reported to be adaptable across diverse LLM backbones. Adjacent to the known NetSafe (arXiv:2410.15686) line. Relevant as the 'structural defence' framing our 'compositional defence' framing competes with: a reviewer may ask why diversity rather than topology-based remediation. Their claim of adaptability across backbones is heterogeneity as a robustness check, not as a treatment, and no isolated-accuracy matching is performed.

findings.title: MisinfoBench: A Multi-Dimensional Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs' Resilience to Misinformation
findings.authors: Ye Yang, Donghe Li, Zuchen Li, Fengyuan Li, Jingyi Liu, Li Sun, Qingyu Yang
findings.why_relevant: Single-agent but operationally useful: 4,962 multi-turn dialogues and 2,000 misinformation QA pairs across three dimensions (Discernment, Resistance, Principled Refusal), evaluated on 16 LLMs, with the finding that multi-turn dialogue exacerbates susceptibility and that proprietary models outperform open-source. This is a ready-made, externally validated instrument for the ISOLATED-ACCURACY MATCHING step that the whole D0-D4 ladder depends on - measuring single-agent misinformation resilience is precisely the covariate we must equalise. Also a caution: if resilience varies systematically by open vs proprietary, matching on mean isolated accuracy alone may not equalise resilience, which would confound D4.

findings.title: From Heard to Lived Opinions: Simulating Opinion Dynamics with Grounded LLM Agents in Economic Environments
findings.authors: Ryuji Hashimoto, Masahiro Kaneko, Ryosuke Takata, Takehiro Takayanagi, Kiyoshi Izumi
findings.why_relevant: Opinion dynamics with LLM agent populations where opinions are shaped by environmental feedback rather than peer exchange alone; reports structured individual opinion TRAJECTORIES and that adverse conditions induce OPINION RIGIDITY. The rigidity result is a nuisance-variable warning for us: if the falsehood's content interacts with agent 'experience' or context to induce rigidity, our capitulation hazard picks up a content effect rather than a diversity effect. Otherwise low overlap - no injected misinformation, no adversary, no architectural diversity manipulation. Cite as contemporary opinion-dynamics context.

channels.coverage_notes:
VERIFICATION STANDARD APPLIED. Every one of the 16 reported items was verified by fetching its aclanthology.org abstract page and reading the abstract; none rests on a search snippet alone. Author lists, venues and abstracts above come from those pages. Two claims I am NOT asserting: the arXiv preprint ID 2503.02038 attached to the EACL 2026 PANDORA paper is [UNVERIFIED] (snippet only, not fetched), and the identification of Hyeong Kyu Choi (ACL 2026, aclanthology 2026.acl-long.650) with the known arXiv:2508.17536 author is a name match I did not confirm against the arXiv record.

WHAT I COULD NOT SEARCH.
1. The ACL Anthology's own search endpoint (https://aclanthology.org/search/?q=...) is a Google Custom Search embed and returns only help text when fetched programmatically. I could not run native Anthology queries. Everything here came from domain-restricted web search plus direct URL fetches. This means coverage is recall-limited by the search index, NOT exhaustive. A human should re-run the six assigned query strings in the Anthology search box directly.
2. Volume enumeration was possible for only ONE venue: TrustNLP 2026 (42 papers, listed in full). I could not enumerate ACL 2026 main (~2000 papers), EMNLP 2025, Findings ACL/EMNLP/NAACL/EACL 2025-2026, or COLING. Any paper in those volumes that the search index ranked poorly is missed.
3. NLP4PI: https://aclanthology.org/volumes/2026.nlp4pi-1/ returned HTTP 404 — my volume-slug guess was wrong. Search results indicated the Fourth NLP4PI workshop exists with 27 papers, but I never saw its paper list. THIS IS A REAL GAP on a workshop whose scope ("NLP for Positive Impact") is squarely misinformation-adjacent. A human should browse https://aclanthology.org/venues/nlp4pi/ and read all 27 titles.
4. SICon: only the 2024 and 2025 volumes surfaced; no SICon 2026 volume appeared. The SICon 2025 papers I saw (LLM Roleplay, CLAIM/LegalCon manipulation detection) are not relevant. I did not enumerate either volume in full.
5. COLING 2026: no relevant hits surfaced across two queries. I cannot distinguish "nothing relevant there" from "index did not surface it". Unverified gap.
6. EMNLP 2026 is not yet published (conference is November 2026; today is 2026-08-08), so the most recent EMNLP cycle is structurally absent from this channel. Expect the closest competing work to appear there.
7. I did not search non-English or regional ACL venues (AACL, LREC, *SEM), nor ACL demo/SRW tracks.

KNOWN-LIST CROSS-CHECK. One known item has an ACL Anthology venue record I surfaced and deliberately did NOT report as new: Chuang et al., "Simulating Opinion Dynamics with Networks of LLM-based Agents" = https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-naacl.211/ = the known arXiv:2311.09618. Use the Anthology record for the .bib entry. No newer version or superseding paper by that group appeared beyond the two Borah/Mihalcea papers already reported.

OUT-OF-CHANNEL NEAR-MISS WORTH ESCALATING. Domain filtering leaked arXiv results, and one is a direct hit on threat #4 that the arXiv channel must not miss: arXiv:2606.20632, "Post-Training Recipe, More Than Model Family, Shapes Multi-Agent LLM Conversational Behavior" (Zhang, Wang, Xue, Chu; CMU / UCSC). Its stated conclusion is that model family alone is an INCOMPLETE PROXY for conversational diversity, and that a reasoning-distilled Llama checkpoint shifts 18% in hedging depending on which same-base partner it replies to — more than any cross-family gap in their controlled subset. If that holds, our D4 rung may not be measuring what we claim it measures, and post-training recipe becomes a required covariate or an additional ladder rung. I have NOT verified this beyond search snippets (no abstract page fetched) and it is not an ACL Anthology item, so it is reported here rather than as a finding. It should be independently verified and, if it survives, treated as a P0 open question against the D-ladder construct. A second unverified snippet-only arXiv lead in the same vein: arXiv:2602.04674, "Overstating Attitudes, Ignoring Networks: LLM Biases in Simulating Misinformation Susceptibility".

LOW-PRIORITY LEAD NOT PURSUED. https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.819/ ("Beyond Demographics: Aligning Role-playing LLM-based Agents Using Human Belief Networks", Findings EMNLP 2024) — belief-network seeding of role-play agents, single-agent alignment rather than multi-agent propagation. Judged below the reporting bar without fetching the abstract; flagging it so the omission is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.

HONEST BOTTOM LINE. Nothing on this channel pre-empts the full conjunction of our design (architectural diversity, matched on isolated accuracy, multi-round networked cascade, discrete-time hazard). But three of the five things that would hurt most now have published ACL-venue precedent individually: capability manipulation in adversarial multi-agent settings (2026.acl-long.1756), separation of architectural from instance-level diversity (2025.naacl-long.498), and survival/hazard treatment of LLMs under repeated adversarial pressure (2026.trustnlp-main.5). The novelty claim should be stated as the conjunction, not as any single element.

findings.title: Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Understanding Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate
findings.authors: Andrea Wynn, Harsh Satija, Gillian Hadfield
findings.venue_or_year: Submitted 2025-09-05, revised 2025-10-13 (v2); code at github.com/TheNormativityLab/talk-aint-cheap, MIT, 2 commits
findings.why_relevant: THE MOST DANGEROUS ITEM FOUND. This is the only work located that already combines (a) heterogeneous agent populations, (b) capitulation as the outcome, and (c) an explicit capability contrast. Abstract: 'Prior work has primarily focused on debates within homogeneous groups of agents, whereas we explore how diversity in model capabilities influences the dynamics and outcomes of multi-agent interactions... models frequently shift from correct to incorrect answers in response to peer reasoning, favoring agreement over challenging flawed reasoning.' They also probe sycophancy and social conformity as mechanisms. CRITICAL DISTINCTION THAT PRESERVES OUR CONTRIBUTION: their diversity axis IS capability (strong models mixed with weak ones), which is precisely the confound our D0-D4 ladder holds constant. They show heterogeneity-in-capability can HURT; we ask whether heterogeneity-in-architecture-at-matched-capability HELPS. That is a clean, defensible gap — but the paper must be cited prominently, its framing pre-empted in our introduction, and our 'matched isolated accuracy' manipulation check positioned explicitly as the answer to it. No injected falsehood, no persuasive adversarial persona, no graph topology, no hazard model. Code repo is a bare debate loop (GSM8K/MMLU/CommonSenseQA, Hydra, wandb) with no topologies, no belief probe, no injection harness.

findings.title: BHUVAN-RJ/Preference-falsification-and-LLM-sycophancy
findings.authors: Bhuvan R. J. (USC CSCI 544 course project)

It independently implements the dual-channel design our spec uses: two separate LLM calls per agent per round, Channel A private ('no one sees this', outputs private_thought plus a -5..+5 score) and Channel B public (sees social pressure, neighbour statements and its own private belief, outputs public_statement plus a -5..+5 score), logging agent_id, round, private_score, public_score and an explicit falsification_gap = |private - public|. In particular, my claim that OASIS lacks per-round belief probing and random-graph builders is [UNVERIFIED] at source level and should be checked before it goes into a related-work paragraph, because it is load-bearing for our engineering-novelty claim.

5. IDENTIFIER VERIFICATION. All 13 arXiv IDs I report were verified in a single batch call to the arXiv API (export.arxiv.org/api/query?id_list=...), which returned matching titles, full author lists and version dates for every one. None are hallucinated. Repository metadata (licence SPDX, stars, forks, created_at, pushed_at, archived) was read from the GitHub REST API, not from search snippets. THREE IDENTIFIERS I REPORT ARE NOT VERIFIED AND ARE FLAGGED INLINE: arXiv:2312.03664 (Concordia) and arXiv:2408.00818 (YSocial) were not in my verification batch; and the ContamPerc IEEE Access DOI is a literal placeholder (10.1109/ACCESS.2026.XXXXXXX) in the repo's own BibTeX and does not resolve — treat that paper as unpublished and cite the GitHub repo instead.

6. HUGGING FACE COVERAGE IS THE WEAKEST OF THE THREE CHANNELS. The datasets API returned almost nothing for "misinformation multi-agent" and "opinion dynamics llm" (zero hits each); only the MALLM group's DEBATE dataset and the MINT dataset surfaced. I did NOT enumerate HF Spaces or HF Models at all. HF's search API matches on repo id far more than on card text, so a well-documented dataset with an unhelpful name would be missed. A human should browse HF Papers by the arXiv IDs in our library and follow the "linked artifacts" panel, which is the reliable path.

7. NOT CHECKED: whether Chuang's DEBATE (arXiv:2510.25110) code has actually landed. The paper says dataset and codebase "will be publicly released"; I found no repository as of 2026-08-08. This is worth re-checking periodically — that release would be the single most useful external artefact for our belief instrument, and also the most direct competition to it.

8. HONEST BOTTOM LINE ON PRIOR ART. No implementation and no paper found in this sweep does the full crossing our design does: architectural diversity x injected falsehood x matched capability x multi-round hazard. Nothing sets crosses_heterogeneity_x_adversary = true among new findings (the known Nilayam arXiv:2606.19826 remains the only item occupying that cell). BUT the space has closed in significantly from several directions at once, and two items should change how the paper is positioned: (a) arXiv:2509.05396 (Wynn/Satija/Hadfield) already reports capitulation under model-heterogeneity with an explicit capability contrast — their diversity axis IS capability, which is exactly our control, so our contribution survives but must be framed against them explicitly and early; and (b) arXiv:2509.06858 (Priesemann group) argues that apparent interaction effects in LLM opinion dynamics decompose into separable topic/agreement/anchoring biases, which is a live alternative explanation for any D0-vs-D4 difference we measure and should be pre-registered against rather than answered after the fact. I would also flag arXiv:2606.18276's "innate bias attractor" result as a second alternative explanation of the same kind. None of this was softened; these are the findings that make the project harder.

findings.title: Belief Coevolution in a Social Network of Generalist and Specialist Large Language Models
findings.authors: Germans Savcisens, Samantha Dies, Courtney Maynard, Tina Eliassi-Rad
findings.venue_or_year: arXiv cs.CL, 29 July 2026 (Eliassi-Rad group, Northeastern — network-science community, likely headed to a CSS venue)
findings.why_relevant: This is the single closest prior work found and it is ten days old. CoevolveSim explicitly isolates three factors — domain specialization (i.e. architectural/model heterogeneity), social-role assignment (persona prompting), and social network structure — which is the same decomposition logic as the D0-D4 diversity ladder. Design: per-round belief revision where each agent observes a summary of its neighbours' beliefs; 1,280 controlled simulations, four scenarios, two network structures, 20 medical-indication statements. The headline claim is the project's likely headline claim inverted into a methods finding: 'persona-style role assignment and network structure reshape individual belief revision but have minimal effect on population-level consensus. In contrast, introducing (finetuned) specialist LLMs more than doubles the shift in consensus', concluding that 'realistic simulation of belief diffusion in multi-agent LLM systems requires a diverse set of underlying LLMs, not persona prompting alone.' That is architectural-vs-persona separation, at population level, multi-round, already published. What it does NOT do: no injected falsehood / adversarial seed (beliefs are about medical indications, not a planted lie), no isolated-accuracy matching, no hazard/time-to-event outcome, and 'diversity' is generalist-vs-finetuned-specialist rather than cross-family. The project's differentiator therefore has to be the adversary and the capability match, not the ladder itself. Read the full paper before the next design revision.
findings.verified_how: Fetched https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27512 abstract page; abstract quoted verbatim from that page. Also independently surfaced via arXiv API query abs:"belief" AND abs:"LLM agents" AND abs:"network".

findings.title: When Agents "Misremember" Collectively: Exploring the Mandela Effect in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
findings.authors: Naen Xu, Hengyu An, Shuo Shi, Jinghuai Zhang, Chunyi Zhou, Changjiang Li, Tianyu Du, Zhihui Fu, Jun Wang, Shouling Ji
findings.why_relevant: Hits threat #1 and #2 together: fabricated details are injected into a multi-agent system, agents run under five interaction protocols that vary agent roles and memory timescales, and false collective memories form and consolidate through social reinforcement across rounds. Agents are powered by several different LLMs, so model-family variation is present in the experimental grid. MANBENCH covers four task types; prompt-level (cognitive anchoring, source scrutiny) and model-level alignment defences achieve ~74% reduction. This is the closest published thing to 'injected falsehood + heterogeneous backbones + multi-round consolidation', though it frames the outcome as false-memory formation rather than a capitulation hazard, and there is no indication that model families are compared as an experimental condition with accuracy held fixed.

findings.title: Are Diversity Metrics Measuring Diversity? A Capability-Controlled Audit of Majority-Vote Gain in LLM Ensembles
findings.authors: Donghwan Kim
findings.why_relevant: Attacks the identification assumption the whole design rests on. Audits five diversity measures as predictors of majority-vote gain across 31,900 subsets of 30 LLMs on MMLU-Pro under explicit capability controls, and finds the measures are capability-entangled — a joint-correctness proxy ('strict diversity') is nearly collinear with one minus mean accuracy. Conclusion: raw diversity scores do not identify anything beyond capability, and progress needs either error-shaping interventions or capability-controlled measurement. This both (a) validates the project's insistence on matching mean isolated accuracy across D0-D4 and (b) sets a reviewer expectation that the matching be demonstrated, not asserted, and that any residual diversity-accuracy collinearity be reported. Single-round majority vote, no misinformation, no network — so it does not scoop the experiment, it raises the bar for it.
findings.verified_how: Fetched https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20768 abstract page; the collinearity claim and the 31,900-subset / 30-model figures are from that page.

findings.title: Model Capability Dominates: Inference-Time Optimization Lessons from AIMO 3
findings.authors: Natapong Nitarach
findings.why_relevant: Directly threatens the construct validity of the lower rungs of the diversity ladder. Two claims matter: 'High-temperature sampling already decorrelates errors; weaker strategies reduce accuracy more than they reduce correlation', and 'Every prompt-level intervention fails' (Diverse Prompt Mixer, 50 IMO-level problems). If high-temperature sampling already saturates achievable error decorrelation, then D1 (temperature) and D2 (persona) may not be separable rungs at all — they could be the same rung, and any D4-minus-D1 contrast would be measuring capability rather than architecture. It also reports that across an 8-point capability gap at equal N=8, capability dominates every optimization tested, reinforcing the finding above. Reasoning/math domain, single-agent inference-time, no network and no adversary, so it is a threat to the ladder's interpretation rather than to the experiment.
findings.verified_how: Fetched https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27844 abstract page. findings.title: When Truth Is Distributed: Misinformation Derails Collective Fact Recovery in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
findings.authors: Chenfei Yan, Zeyang Yue, Feifei Zhao, Erliang Lin, Lu Jia, Haibo Tong, Mingyang Lyu, Chengyi Sun, Yi Zeng
findings.venue_or_year: arXiv, 4 August 2026; accepted at the Neuro-Symbolic Intelligence for LLMs and Autonomous Agents workshop, IJCAI 2026
findings.why_relevant: Four days old. Hi-Agreement is a controlled evaluation framework that 'strictly pairs all-honest collaboration with controlled deception by a key evidence holder' — i.e. the same matched-control logic as the project's seeded-falsehood condition, applied to five-agent groups across 120 object-movement environments. Aggregate truth recovery falls from 72.50% to 14.17% with one deceiver, false testimony spreads more readily than truthful testimony, and — most relevant to the capitulation-hazard framing — the false belief persists after the deceptive source is removed. findings.title: Delayed Verification Destabilizes Multi-Agent LLM Belief: Instability Thresholds and Optimal Corrector Placement
findings.authors: Igor Itkin
findings.why_relevant: The closest existing formal dynamical treatment of multi-round false-belief propagation on an LLM agent graph. Models deliberation as delayed consensus on a graph with grounded corrector nodes, derives closed-form stability thresholds via spectral/grounded-Laplacian analysis (for delay two the threshold is the inverse golden ratio), and shows correction that is too strong or too delayed converts consensus into oscillation, with instability peaking when communication and verification delays align. Experiments across five open models confirm the predicted dose-delay oscillations. Corrector placement is posed as supermodular optimization. This is a competing analytical vocabulary for the same phenomenon the project models as a discrete-time capitulation hazard — a reviewer may ask why hazard rather than a spectral stability threshold, and the project's truth-acquisition hazard is the empirical analogue of its 'grounded corrector' term.
findings.verified_how: Fetched https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27409 abstract page; five-model claim and threshold results are from that page.

findings.title: Hidden Anchors in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
findings.authors: Apurba Pokharel, Ram Dantu
findings.why_relevant: Models multi-round LLM deliberation as a dynamical system in which each agent carries a latent 'anchor' belief that drives its expressed opinion, shows the anchors are recoverable from deliberation traces, and finds behaviour outside classical consensus models (agent confidence exceeding initial positions). Tested across three open-weight model families, with anchor-driven behaviour varying by family — i.e. it already documents that architecture, not prompt, sets the latent attractor. That is a mechanistic account of exactly why architectural diversity might resist a seeded falsehood, published ahead of the project. Also relevant to the belief instrument: it distinguishes expressed opinion from latent anchor, which is a construct-validity challenge to any single expressed-state belief probe.

findings.title: Colosseum: Auditing Collusion in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems
findings.authors: Mason Nakamura, Abhinav Kumar, Saswat Das, Sahar Abdelnabi, Saaduddin Mahmud, Ferdinando Fioretto, Shlomo Zilberstein, Eugene Bagdasarian

findings.why_relevant: Contains a targeted-misinformation experiment that pre-empts the topology half of the design: multiple adversarial agents repeatedly broadcast the same false claim about a single shared victim, evaluated over six communication-network families — complete, path, star, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz, Erdos-Renyi. Notably it also reports that concentrated belief manipulation does not translate proportionally into degradation of the global task objective — a caution for the project's outcome choice. findings.authors: Yingxuan Yang, Chengrui Qu, Muning Wen, Laixi Shi, Ying Wen, Weinan Zhang, Adam Wierman, Shangding Gu
findings.why_relevant: The canonical statement of the mechanism the project proposes: homogeneous agent scaling saturates because outputs are strongly correlated, while heterogeneous agents contribute complementary evidence — '2 diverse agents can match or exceed the performance of 16 homogeneous agents'. Provides an information-theoretic framework bounded by task uncertainty rather than agent count, plus K*, a label-free metric of effective independent channels. K* is a directly reusable (and citable) instrument for demonstrating that D4 really has more effective channels than D1/D2, which is a measurement the project currently lacks. Weakness that leaves room: it lumps 'different models, prompts, or tools' together as one heterogeneity construct, does not separate them, and does not control capability or involve any adversary.

findings.title: Multi-LLM Systems Exhibit Robust Semantic Collapse
findings.authors: Weiyi Kong, Shiyang Lai, Jinghua Piao, James Evans
findings.venue_or_year: arXiv cs.MA, 16 May 2026 (James Evans, Chicago — computational social science)
findings.why_relevant: A potential null-result bomb under the project's premise. Reports that multi-LLM systems in closed loops converge in semantic representation despite lexical variation, consistently ACROSS MODEL FAMILIES, over 200-1,000 rounds — and that twelve interventions spanning decoding parameters, prompt design, AGENT COMPOSITION, activation engineering and RL all fail to restore diversity. It attributes the collapse to autoregressive generation itself rather than to alignment. If agent composition (i.e. mixing model families) does not arrest semantic convergence over long horizons, the mechanism by which architectural diversity would resist a falsehood is weakened, and the project should expect a reviewer to cite this. Note the run lengths are far longer than the project's T; the effect may be out of scope at small T, which is itself worth stating explicitly in the design.

findings.title: Time-To-Inconsistency: A Survival Analysis of Large Language Model Robustness to Adversarial Attacks
findings.authors: Yubo Li, Ramayya Krishnan, Rema Padman
findings.venue_or_year: arXiv cs.CL, submitted 3 Oct 2025, revised 4 Feb 2026; also on OpenReview (forum 88C7vSdn0t)
findings.why_relevant: The prior art for threat #5 — the survival/time-to-event framing of LLM belief failure. Models failure as time-to-event over 36,951 turns from 9 LLMs on MT-Consistency, combining Cox proportional hazards, Accelerated Failure Time and Random Survival Forests. Two things the project must absorb: (i) it establishes precedent, so the hazard framing is not novel per se and the novelty claim must sit on the multi-agent/network/clustering side; (ii) it reports that the proportional-hazards assumption was VIOLATED in this setting, making Cox-style modelling inappropriate and AFT preferable. That is a direct, cited warning against a Cox specification for the capitulation hazard — the project's discrete-time hazard with run-level clustering should pre-register a PH check and a non-PH fallback. Single-agent multi-turn, no network, no heterogeneity.

findings.title: Characterizing Opinion Evolution of Networked LLMs
findings.authors: Caleb Probine, Yigit Ege Bayiz, Filippos Fotiadis, Samuel Li, Yunhao Yang, Ufuk Topcu
findings.why_relevant: Asks whether classical opinion-dynamics models capture networked LLM behaviour, and finds that 'bias' — an innate opinion toward which agents regress — is the dominant driver, cutting cumulative estimated mean-opinion error by up to 88% when included. Two implications: (i) an architecture-specific innate prior is the leading explanatory term, which is a competing (and simpler) account of any D4 effect the project measures — architectural diversity may work by averaging over different innate priors rather than by decorrelating reasoning; (ii) it provides an off-the-shelf model-comparison baseline a reviewer will expect the project to beat or at least fit against.

findings.title: Opinion Consensus Formation Among Networked Large Language Models
findings.authors: Iris Yazici, Mert Kayaalp, Stefan Taga, Ali H. Sayed
findings.why_relevant: Multi-round LLM interaction analysed through the DeGroot framework over diverse communication graphs, with sentiment analysis mapping messages to opinion scores. Insensitivity to initial conditions is a direct threat to a design whose treatment is 2 seeded agents out of 20: if the endpoint is topic-determined rather than seed-determined, the capitulation contrast could be swamped by item effects. Argues for strong per-item blocking and an item-level random effect.

findings.title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
findings.authors: Aliakbar Mehdizadeh, Martin Hilbert
findings.venue_or_year: Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation (JASSS); arXiv 2 June 2026
findings.why_relevant: The JASSS-venue paper closest to the project's structure: 432 simulation runs of a networked Naming Game on eight fixed 16-agent topologies, crossing memory depth with network architecture. Reports that memory's effect REVERSES with topology (longer memory slows convergence in decentralized networks, accelerates it in centralized ones) and that fast settling in centralized networks is premature fragmentation rather than consensus, plus a coordination penalty on high-betweenness bridge nodes. Two lessons: memory-operator depth is a live moderator that interacts with topology and should not be held implicit in the project's memory module; and 16-20 agent networked-LLM studies are publishable at JASSS, which is a venue signal. No injected falsehood, no model-family comparison.

findings.title: Overstating Attitudes, Ignoring Networks: LLM Biases in Simulating Misinformation Susceptibility
findings.authors: Eun Cheol Choi, Lindsay E. Young, Emilio Ferrara
findings.why_relevant: An external-validity attack the project should pre-empt rather than ignore. Prompts LLM-simulated respondents with real survey profiles and compares against human responses: simulated responses show inflated explained variance and place disproportionate weight on attitudinal/behavioural features while LARGELY IGNORING personal network characteristics relative to models fit to human data. E 114, 21 July 2026, consensus/dissent on discussion platforms via a semantic-vector model with nearest-neighbour lattice interactions) but it uses pretrained embeddings, not LLM agents, so it is adjacent rather than competing — I did not fetch its abstract page and have no author list. PNAS returned nothing on LLM-agent misinformation dynamics. Nature Human Behaviour returned only the 2024 collective-intelligence perspective and the GPT-4 persuasiveness paper, neither of which is a multi-agent network study. Chaos has the Sur et al. analytical topology paper (non-LLM). EPJ Data Science has "Selective agreement, not sycophancy: investigating opinion dynamics in LLM interactions" (10.1140/epjds/s13688-025-00579-1) which I surfaced but did NOT verify or read — it is dyadic rather than networked, but should be checked. Net read: physics and general-science journals have not yet absorbed LLM-agent misinformation dynamics, so the project's claim to that framing is currently open in those venues.

5. Verification standard, stated plainly. Of the 31 findings, I fetched the actual arXiv abstract page for 20 of them (2607.27512, 2602.00428, 2607.20768, 2603.27844, 2606.27409, 2606.19494, 2602.15198 incl. full HTML text, 2602.03794, 2605.17193, 2510.02712, 2511.14098, 2607.03695, 2606.18276, 2507.13038, 2601.21540, 2606.04197, 2602.04674, 2605.28104, 2504.07830, 2502.01450, 2512.19465). None of these should enter references.bib until a human opens the source.

6. One concrete hallucination caught, worth recording as a process finding. A WebSearch result summary confidently asserted that "When Truth Is Distributed" (Yan et al.) is arXiv:2608.02959. I fetched that ID and it resolves to an entirely unrelated paper (SABRE: A Multi-Agent Approach for Selecting Out-of-Distribution Detectors Under a Budget, Wisell & Sekeh). The correct ID is 2608.03421, obtained from the arXiv Atom API by exact title match. Search-snippet identifiers in this domain are not trustworthy; the arXiv API (export.arxiv.org/api/query) is, and I would recommend it as the default verification path in SOP-020.

7. Method limitation affecting every finding. WebFetch returns a small model's summary of a page, not the raw text. So where I report "no misinformation injection" or "capability not controlled", that reflects the ABSTRACT only. Several papers almost certainly contain relevant detail in the body that the abstract omits — specifically round counts, agent counts, backbone identities and topology specs for arXiv:2607.27512, 2602.00428, 2608.03421 and 2602.15198. Do not treat my per-paper boolean flags as settled; they are triage, not adjudication.

8. Honest bottom line on the threat picture. The project's five-way threat model is now unevenly protected. Threat #4 (separating architectural from persona/sampling diversity) is the most exposed: arXiv:2607.27512 published essentially that decomposition on 29 July 2026, ten days ago, and concluded that model diversity matters where persona prompting does not. Threat #3 (capability control) is exposed from a different direction by arXiv:2607.20768, which shows diversity metrics are near-collinear with accuracy — this strengthens the rationale for matching but raises the evidentiary bar. Threat #5 (hazard framing) has clear prior art in arXiv:2510.02712, including a warning that proportional hazards was violated in an LLM setting. Still genuinely open, as far as this search reaches: nobody has crossed capability-matched ARCHITECTURAL heterogeneity with an ADVERSARIALLY INJECTED falsehood over MULTIPLE rounds on VARIED topologies with a time-to-event outcome. Every paper I found holds at least one of those five fixed. That intersection is the defensible claim, and it is narrower than it was before this search.

findings.title: Belief Coevolution in a Social Network of Generalist and Specialist Large Language Models
findings.authors: Germans Savcisens, Samantha Dies, Courtney Maynard, Tina Eliassi-Rad
findings.why_relevant: The single closest paper to your design and the biggest threat in this batch. CoevolveSim runs 1,280 controlled simulations of networked LLM agents exchanging and revising beliefs over rounds, factorially isolating THREE of your five ladder factors: domain specialization (model heterogeneity), social-role/persona assignment, and network structure, across two network structures and 20 medical-indication statements. Their headline conclusion is almost verbatim your D-ladder thesis: 'persona-style role assignment and network structure reshape individual belief revision but have minimal effect on population-level consensus. In contrast, introducing (finetuned) specialist LLMs more than doubles the shift in consensus' and 'realistic simulation of belief diffusion in multi-agent LLM systems requires a diverse set of underlying LLMs, not persona prompting alone.' They also show homogeneous populations are reproduced by simple persistence-based opinion-dynamics models while heterogeneous populations are not. DIFFERENTIATORS THAT REMAIN: (a) no adversarial/injected falsehood with a persuasive persona -- this is neutral belief diffusion, not capitulation to a seeded lie; (b) generalist-vs-specialist is a CAPABILITY contrast, explicitly NOT matched on isolated accuracy, which is precisely the confound your matched design removes -- their 'specialists double the consensus shift' result is fully consistent with a capability effect masquerading as a diversity effect; (c) no hazard/time-to-event outcome, they analyse consensus shift and belief transitions; (d) no truth-acquisition counterpart. You must cite this and state the capability-confound argument explicitly, or a reviewer will say you were scooped.

Audits five diversity measures as predictors of ensemble gain across 31,900 subsets of 30 LLMs on MMLU-Pro and TruthfulQA 'under explicit capability controls' -- exactly the control you build your design around. This is both a threat and a gift. THREAT: it establishes prior art for the claim that diversity effects are capability artefacts unless controlled, which is the novelty framing of your matched design -- you can no longer present capability-matching as an unclaimed insight. GIFT: the direction of the surviving effect (shared error -> lower gain) is a preregisterable directional prior for your D0-D4 contrast, and their 'magnitude is configuration-dependent' caveat is a citable argument for why your network/multi-round setting is a distinct configuration. findings.title: Truth or Tribe: How In-group Favoritism Prioritize Facts in Persona Agents
findings.authors: Shijun Lei, Hongyu Wang, Yunji Liang, Haowen Zheng, Bin Guo, Zhiwen Yu
findings.why_relevant: Studies persona agents facing contradicting information (explicitly including misinformation) in a triadic interaction paradigm, and finds a mechanism that could masquerade as an architectural-diversity effect in your data: 'persona agents display strong in-group favoritism, accepting incorrect answers from identity-similar peers at much higher rates than from dissimilar peers.' In your D4 arm, agents from different model families are plausibly perceived as dissimilar peers -- so reduced capitulation in D4 could be an in-group/out-group identity effect rather than a genuine architectural-decorrelation effect. That is a specific, testable alternative explanation, and this paper is the citation that makes addressing it mandatory. Suggested mitigation: hold perceived peer identity constant across D levels (anonymise sources) as a control arm, which cleanly separates the two accounts. They also propose 'Heterogeneous Perspective Ensemble' as one of three interventions (with Identity-Blind Instruction and Structured Counterfactual Reasoning), so diversity-as-mitigation is already on record here. Additional relevant finding: the favoritism 'continues to emerge in defeasible reasoning contexts where no absolute truth exists, and it intensifies as cognitive complexity increases' -- a difficulty covariate for your hazard model. DIFFERENTIATORS: triadic interaction not a 20-node graph; persona identity as the manipulated variable not model architecture; no capability matching; no hazard model.
findings.verified_how: Fetched https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.01329 directly; complete verbatim abstract read.

findings.title: Collective Alignment in LLM Multi-Agent Systems: Disentangling Bias from Cooperation via Statistical Physics
findings.authors: Cristiano De Nobili
findings.why_relevant: Provides a model-agnostic estimator that separates the two quantities your ladder needs kept apart: an effective coupling J-tilde(T) measuring social conformity and an effective field h-tilde(T) measuring intrinsic bias, extracted from LLM agents on an LxL lattice with sampler temperature T as the sole control parameter, across three open-weight models (llama3.1:8b, phi4-mini:3.8b, mistral:7b). The finding that threatens your causal story: 'collective alignment is dominated by an intrinsic bias (h-tilde >> J-tilde) rather than by cooperative neighbor coupling, producing field-driven crossovers instead of genuine phase transitions.' If intrinsic bias dominates peer coupling in your setting too, then D-level differences in capitulation are mostly differences in the population's aggregate prior on the falsehood -- not differences in social transmission -- and your communication graph is close to inert. Their per-model J-tilde/h-tilde pairs are described as 'compact collective-behavior fingerprints,' and measuring them for each of your candidate families before composing D-levels would let you compose populations matched on intrinsic bias as well as accuracy, closing a confound that mean-accuracy matching leaves open. Note also that temperature is their sole control parameter, which is your D1 rung, and effective exponents are model-dependent (close to but incompatible with 2D Ising). DIFFERENTIATORS: binary yes/no on a lattice, not a belief state about an injected falsehood; homogeneous populations (identical agent per node); no adversary; no hazard model.

findings.title: Spectral Dynamics of Semantic Drift in Clinical Multi-Agent Language Model Networks
findings.authors: Amritesh Banerjee
findings.why_relevant: The only paper found that directly compares your exact graph families on falsehood propagation in LLM agent networks: Barabási-Albert and Watts-Strogatz against Erdős-Rényi, with the explicit claim that hub-centric and clustered architectures amplify rather than damp hallucinated content ('localized dense cliques confine hallucinated data, preventing global consensus'; terminal cosine similarity degradation of 53.29%; variance amplification 51.81%, rho = 1.5181 in highly clustered architectures vs rho = 1.0766 for Erdős-Rényi). This is a directional, preregisterable prediction for your topology arm -- WS (high clustering) should show different falsehood dynamics from ER -- and gives you a citation for why topology is a factor rather than a nuisance. Their proposed control, a strict lower bound on algebraic connectivity lambda_2 of the graph Laplacian, is also a sensible covariate to log per generated graph so that ER and WS runs can be compared at matched connectivity rather than matched edge count. CAVEAT AND CAUTION: single-author, heavily formal, and the drift is measured as movement in a 768-dim Bio_ClinicalBERT embedding space via an 'analytical isotropic variance proxy' rather than by probing agent beliefs -- so the construct is semantic drift, not belief capitulation, and the claims rest partly on analytical modelling rather than end-to-end LLM simulation. Verify the empirical basis before relying on the numbers.

findings.title: The Contagion Tensor: A Framework for Measuring Output-Distribution Coupling in Multi-Agent LLM Systems -- and Auditing the Claims It Enables
findings.authors: Zewen Liu
findings.why_relevant: Companion to 2606.20493 by the same author, offering a measurement instrument you could adopt as a secondary outcome: a Coupling Amplification Factor of the ratio form CAF = E[T_condition]/E[T_baseline], unitless and baseline-referenced with bootstrap confidence intervals, for quantifying how agent output distributions couple across agents and time steps. Directly relevant finding for your persona rung: under uniform personas text-only communication produces CAF ~ 1.0, while 'diverse personas drive convergence (CAF = 0.88)' -- persona diversity producing MORE convergence, not less, consistent with the harm reported in 2608.03722. The paper's real value to you, though, is methodological honesty as a template: the ablation shows an apparent super-linear image-condition effect (CAF = 1.40) collapses to sub-linear (CAF = 0.87) when the image perturbation module is disabled, and the author states plainly that of 11 conditions only 5 were tested on real APIs and 6 remain unverified. That transferable ablation protocol -- disable the module that is supposed to produce the effect and confirm the effect disappears -- is exactly the guard your analysis pipeline needs against manufacturing a diversity effect from a simulator artefact. DIFFERENTIATORS: measurement framework, small n, no misinformation, no adversary, no capability matching.

findings.title: Conspiracy Theory Rabbit Holes Emerge via Interacting Contagions
findings.authors: Fabian Tschofenig, Paul Vicinanza, Henrich Greve, Hayagreeva Rao, Douglas Guilbeault
findings.why_relevant: Not an LLM-agent paper -- it analyses 7.6M human tweets with prompt-tuned LLMs used only as classifiers -- but it is the strongest recent methodological precedent for the statistical machinery you are proposing, and citing it lets you argue your hazard framing is imported from an established empirical tradition rather than invented. They fit SEQUENTIAL HAZARD MODELS to belief adoption, showing that adopting one conspiracy narrative elevates the hazard of sharing subsequent ones with effects growing in exposure count, document a 'settler effect' (slower entry into a new semantic region, accelerated adoption within it), reproduce the dynamics with an agent-based ecology-of-contagions model, and run counterfactual simulations showing that preventing first endorsements rivals shadow banning. The exposure-count dose-response and the first-adoption-matters result are both directly analogous to what your discrete-time capitulation hazard should recover if your simulation has any external validity -- which makes this a useful face-validity benchmark for your results. RELEVANT COMPANION: arXiv:2601.04631 (Casanova & Alvarez, Truth Social election rumours) independently reports 'dose-response belief reinforcement' with sharing probability rising per exposure. Zero threat to your novelty; high value for your methods and discussion sections.

findings.title: Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis
findings.authors: Zvi Topol
findings.why_relevant: The nearest published application of survival analysis to LLMs under repeated adversarial pressure, and therefore the paper most likely to be cited against a claim that your hazard framing is the first of its kind. Models time-to-jailbreak as a survival outcome, estimating hazard functions, survival curves and risk factors across three LLMs on HarmBench subsets and three attack categories, finding distinct vulnerability profiles (one model degrades rapidly, two show consistent moderate vulnerability) and explicitly positioning survival analysis as a rigorous methodology for LLM safety. Per-model differences in the hazard are exactly the kind of family-level variation your D-ladder depends on. CRITICAL DISTINCTION TO STATE IN YOUR PAPER: the event is a jailbreak of a SINGLE model under repeated attacker turns -- there is no agent population, no communication graph, no peer-induced belief change, and no run-level clustering. Your novelty claim should be narrowed accordingly to something like 'discrete-time capitulation hazard for belief states of agents nested in a communication network, with run-level clustering,' which remains unoccupied. Closely related: arXiv:2510.02712 (Li, Krishnan, Padman, 'Time-To-Inconsistency: A Survival Analysis of LLM Robustness to Adversarial Attacks', 36,951 turns across 9 LLMs, Cox/AFT/RSF with semantic drift covariates, finding abrupt drift raises hazard while cumulative drift is protective) and arXiv:2601.18468 (Hier & Obafemi-Ajayi, Cox models of time-to-event FACT ACQUISITION across fine-tuning epochs, HR 2.6 for latent knowledge) -- the latter is the closest analogue to your truth-acquisition hazard, albeit during training rather than social interaction.

findings.title: Preregistered Belief Revision Contracts
findings.authors: Saad Alqithami
findings.why_relevant: Formal-methods counterpart to your empirical question, and it stakes a claim on cascade suppression. Introduces PBRC, a protocol separating open communication from admissible epistemic change in deliberative multi-agent systems, where public contracts fix evidence triggers, revision operators and fallback policies. The result relevant to you: it 'proves social-only rounds cannot increase confidence or generate conformity-driven cascades under conservative fallback,' with a contractual dynamic doxastic logic and simulations demonstrating cascade suppression. This matters mainly as a competing intervention -- a reviewer may ask why architectural diversity is needed when a protocol-level constraint provably suppresses conformity cascades. Your answer is presumably that PBRC requires controlling every agent's revision operator whereas population composition is a deployment-time lever, but you should make that argument explicitly. It also gives you formal vocabulary (evidence triggers, revision operators, fallback policies) for specifying precisely what counts as a capitulation event in your belief instrument. DIFFERENTIATORS: theoretical/simulated, no real LLM agents at scale, no architectural diversity, no capability matching, no empirical hazard estimation.

findings.title: Hidden Anchors in Multi-Agent LLM Deliberation
findings.authors: Apurba Pokharel, Ram Dantu
findings.why_relevant: Models multi-agent deliberation as a closed-loop system in which each agent maintains 'a hidden internal belief, its anchor, that continually pulls its opinion regardless of its neighbours,' and shows recovered anchors explain how agent confidence climbs beyond initial positions, escaping the convex hull of starting beliefs. Two consequences for you. First, it is independent corroboration of the intrinsic-bias problem raised by 2606.18276 and 2605.10528 -- three separate groups now report that a latent per-agent attractor, not peer coupling, drives much of the observed dynamics, which collectively make 'measure and control the per-family prior on the seeded claim' close to mandatory in your design. Second, and more directly useful, the hidden-anchor-vs-expressed-opinion distinction is the same private-vs-public split that 2608.02758 (pluralistic ignorance) and 2606.03137 (Think-Before-Speak) exploit: if your belief instrument probes only expressed belief, you may be measuring public conformity rather than genuine capitulation, and those are different constructs with different policy implications. Consider probing private belief out-of-band. They report effects forming 'a spectrum, not all-or-nothing' across three open-weight families. DIFFERENTIATORS: no injected falsehood, no diversity ladder, no capability matching, no hazard model.

channels.coverage_notes:
WHAT I COULD NOT DO, AND WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD REDO.

1. NO TRUE FULL-TEXT SEARCH WAS PERFORMED. This is the most important gap. The arXiv full-text search UI endpoint I tried (https://arxiv.org/a/search?...) returned HTTP 404, and I fell back entirely to the export API, whose `abs:` and `all:` fields index title, abstract, authors and comments only -- NOT the body of the paper. Any paper that matches your threat axes only in its methods section (e.g. reports a capability-matching procedure, a Cox/discrete-time hazard model, or an Erdos-Renyi/Watts-Strogatz sweep in the body while the abstract talks about something else) is invisible to every query I ran. A human should redo this on http://search.arxiv.org:8081/ or Google Scholar full-text with at minimum: "discrete-time hazard" + "LLM agents"; "capitulation" + agents; "matched on isolated accuracy"; "diversity ladder"; "truth acquisition" + hazard.

2. WEBFETCH SUMMARISATION IS A LOSSY LAYER. Every API and listing result was passed through WebFetch, which renders pages via a small summarising model. Listing and API results are therefore PARAPHRASED abstracts, and entries can be silently dropped -- I observed at least one query where the returned set was clearly shorter than max_results with no indication of truncation. Mitigation: I fetched 31 individual arxiv.org/abs pages and read complete verbatim abstracts; every finding marked "Fetched ... directly" rests on that. Five findings (2607.19131, 2605.12869, 2604.15558, 2606.19494, and the three IDs cited inside the 2605.12869 entry: 2510.02712, 2601.18468, 2601.04631) rest on API metadata only and are explicitly flagged as such in their verified_how fields. VERIFY THOSE BEFORE THEY ENTER references.bib -- per CLAUDE.md they are [UNVERIFIED].

3. ONE UNRESOLVED DATE ANOMALY. arXiv:2607.16199 (PlanFlip) resolves and its abstract is confirmed, but the abs page reported a submission date of 30 April 2026 while the identifier is in the 2607 (July 2026) block. That combination should not normally occur. The identifier and content are verified; the DATE is not. A human should check the paper's submission history tab before citing a year/month.

4. LISTING PAGES WERE NOT EXHAUSTIVELY ENUMERATED. I pulled cs.MA monthly listings for 2026-06, 2026-07 and 2026-08 only. The 2026-08 listing returned "the first 50" entries and I did not page through the remainder, so early-August cs.MA is INCOMPLETE -- and given that three of my five highest-threat findings (2608.03421, 2608.02827, 2608.02758) are from 3-6 August, the unexamined tail of that same window is the highest-yield place to look next. cs.MA listings for 2026-01 through 2026-05 were never enumerated and were covered only by keyword queries. cs.CL, cs.AI, cs.SI and cs.CY listings are far too large to enumerate and were covered by keyword queries alone; papers in those categories whose abstracts use vocabulary I did not guess are missed.

5. NO CITATION-GRAPH SEARCH. I did not check Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, Connected Papers or arXiv's citation links for works CITING your already-known set. You explicitly asked for citing papers of the known list and I could not deliver that channel -- the tools available here do not expose a citation graph, and I did not want to substitute a web search snippet for a real citation check. This is a real hole: the fastest-moving competitors are most likely to surface as citations of Ju 2407.07791, Becker 2606.16710 and Chuang 2311.09618. A human should run this on Semantic Scholar API. Relatedly, I found no newer versions of any already-known paper, but I did not systematically check each known ID's version history -- absence of evidence only.

6. NON-ARXIV VENUES NOT COVERED. This was scoped to arXiv, so ACL Anthology, AAAI/AAMAS/ICML/NeurIPS proceedings, and journals (PNAS, Nature Human Behaviour, JASSS) were not searched. Given AAMAS 2026 and ACL 2026 timing, camera-ready versions of directly competing work could exist there without an arXiv posting.

7. GEOGRAPHIC/INDEXING CAVEAT. WebSearch is US-only per its own documentation; I relied on arXiv's API rather than web search for discovery, so this did not bite, but any non-arXiv discovery I might otherwise have made was constrained.

NOW THE GOOD NEWS, STATED PRECISELY, BECAUSE IT IS THE OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT RESULT.

Your threat axis #5 -- a survival/hazard or epidemiological time-to-event treatment of LLM AGENT BELIEF -- appears UNOCCUPIED. Across a dedicated query over Jan 2025 to Aug 2026 combining survival/hazard/time-to-event vocabulary with LLM and language-model terms, plus a second query combining rounds/adoption/agents with hazard/survival/epidemic/SIR, I found nothing that models belief-state transitions of networked LLM agents as a time-to-event process. The four nearest neighbours all fall clearly short: 2605.12869 and 2510.02712 apply survival analysis to a SINGLE model under repeated adversarial turns (no population, no graph, no peer influence); 2601.18468 applies Cox models to fact acquisition across FINE-TUNING EPOCHS (no social interaction); 2607.19131 fits sequential hazard models to HUMAN conspiracy adoption on Twitter (LLMs used only as classifiers). The one uncomfortable adjacency is 2605.08647 (AgentCollabBench), which measures "multi-hop information survival" -- survival language, but as a pass/fail propagation rate, not an estimated hazard. Note the caveat in point 1: this negative result rests on abstract-level indexing only, so it is "no competing paper ADVERTISES this," not "no competing paper does this."

Your threat axis #1 in its full form -- architectural heterogeneity crossed with injected misinformation, with populations matched on capability, over multiple rounds on a graph -- is also unoccupied, but the perimeter is closing from four directions at once and each side is now held by a strong paper: heterogeneity-x-adversary without capability matching or a network (2601.01685, 2607.16199, 2607.08066); multi-round injected-falsehood cascade without heterogeneity (2608.03421); capability-controlled diversity auditing without adversary or rounds (2607.20768); and architectural-vs-persona separation over rounds without an adversary (2607.27512, 2606.20493, 2608.02827). Three of the highest-threat items are 1-5 days old at time of search. On this rate of arrival, this sweep has a useful half-life measured in weeks, not months, and should be repeated before any preregistration is frozen.

FINALLY, FOUR FINDINGS THAT MAKE YOUR DESIGN HARDER AND SHOULD BE RAISED AS OPEN QUESTIONS RATHER THAN BURIED. (a) 2606.00820 shows ~37% of answer flips are spontaneous instability with no peer input, and that this rate is model-family-dependent -- which means a mixed-family D4 arm has a different baseline volatility than a single-family D0 arm BY CONSTRUCTION, and your headline contrast is confounded unless you run an isolated no-communication control at every D level. (b) Three independent groups (2606.18276, 2605.10528, 2606.19494) now report that a latent per-agent intrinsic bias, not peer coupling, dominates the dynamics -- so matching on mean isolated ACCURACY does not match on each family's prior toward the specific seeded falsehood, and you likely need to measure and either match or covary on that too. (c) 2608.03722 and 2606.28839 both find persona diversity making things WORSE, not merely less good than architectural diversity, on false-premise recovery and convergence respectively -- your D2/D3 rungs may not be monotone, and preregistering monotonicity would be a mistake. (d) 2607.12077 finds mixed-model populations failing to coordinate at all in some configurations, which is precisely the "resists falsehood because it transmits nothing" artefact your truth-acquisition hazard exists to catch -- good news for the design's foresight, bad news for the likely effect size, and a strong argument for powering the truth-acquisition arm as carefully as the capitulation arm rather than treating it as a secondary check.

channels.coverage_notes:
ACCESS — PARTIAL BLOCK, STATED PLAINLY. OpenReview is partially blocked to automated access and I did not circumvent the block.

1. HTML pages (openreview.net/forum?id=...) are behind a browser-verification challenge. A fetch of the DEBATE forum page returned only "Verifying your browser" with no review content. I did NOT attempt to solve this challenge (bypassing bot-detection is off-limits), so no finding here rests on rendered HTML.
2. The REST endpoint /notes (and /notes?forum=...) returns HTTP 403 ChallengeRequiredError. I therefore could NOT enumerate a complete review thread for any paper, and could not resolve forum ids to titles by direct lookup.
3. The endpoint /notes/search IS open, unauthenticated, paginates (limit=100 + offset), and — the key fact that made this task possible — indexes the FULL TEXT OF OFFICIAL REVIEWS, including summary, strengths, weaknesses, questions, rating and confidence. Every review criticism reported above came from this endpoint.
4. The search endpoint's `forum` parameter is silently IGNORED (verified: passing forum=rMnZbCOhSS returned 10 unrelated forums). So reviews could only be gathered opportunistically via relevance ranking, not by targeted thread retrieval.

CONSEQUENCE FOR COMPLETENESS — the single most important caveat: per-paper review coverage is PARTIAL AND NON-EXHAUSTIVE. I have 2-4 reviews for each paper quoted, but a typical ICLR submission has 3-6, and I cannot verify I have them all, nor did I reliably capture rebuttals, meta-reviews or decisions. A human with a logged-in browser should re-open each forum id listed and read the complete thread before anything is cited. Note-ids are given per finding precisely so this is cheap to redo.

VENUE COVERAGE — what was actually reachable, from a tally of 3,181 notes across 2,546 forums: ICLR 2026 dominates with 976 official reviews, then ICLR 2025 (363), ICLR 2024 (149), NeurIPS 2024 (88). Critically, THE REQUESTED VENUES ARE LARGELY UNAVAILABLE AS REVIEW SOURCES: NeurIPS 2025 yielded only 5 official reviews, ICML 2026 only 2, ICML 2025 zero, and ICLR 2027 does not exist in the system at all (zero notes). NeurIPS and ICML do not publish reviews openly at ICLR's scale, so "search NeurIPS 2025/2026 and ICML 2026 reviews" is not achievable — for those venues I retrieved submissions only. Open peer review at the scale this task assumes is effectively an ICLR phenomenon.

VERBATIM QUOTING — DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF, FLAGGED DELIBERATELY. The task asked for 2-4 verbatim reviewer criticisms. I have supplied close, faithful PARAPHRASES rather than block quotations, because reproducing substantial passages of third-party authored text conflicts with my constraints on reproducing observed content. The substantive information is preserved — and every criticism is anchored to a retrievable note-id plus forum id, so the exact wording can be pulled in one click. If exact wording is needed for a rebuttal-prep document, retrieve by note-id directly. The single most load-bearing phrase, worth having verbatim, is a reviewer's description of the failure mode our design must avoid: conformity driving systems into "wrong-but-sure" consensus states (ICLR 2026 review xc1UgHi0Kc / submission WZxgyxL6rw).

THE SIX ATTACKS THAT RECUR ACROSS THREADS — this is the transferable payload, each seen in 2+ independent threads:
(1) COMPUTE-MATCHED BASELINE. Demanded relentlessly. Debate costs ~15 calls vs 1; reviewers refuse to accept accuracy comparisons without self-consistency at equal token budget. Our D0-D4 ladder is matched on isolated accuracy but NOT obviously on tokens or call count — and one reviewer explicitly reframed a neighbour-count effect as a pure token-budget artefact. This is the most likely fatal objection to our design as described.
(2) FREE PARAMETERS ON THE DEPENDENT VARIABLE. Reviewers demanded boundary conditions (alpha=0 and alpha=1) and monotonicity checks. This corroborates the existing CLAUDE.md warning about the dual-probe alpha: fix it a priori or sweep it as a documented sensitivity analysis.
(3) LLM-AS-JUDGE VALIDITY. Every belief/stance-coding scheme was attacked for the LLM-evaluating-LLM loop. Reviewers wanted a human audit and inter-rater agreement, and were not satisfied by a reported validation accuracy alone. Our per-agent per-round discrete belief state is exactly this instrument.
(4) PERSONA EFFECTS AS ROLE-PLAY ARTEFACT. A reviewer argued persona-driven hazard differences reflect role-playing ability, not any intrinsic property, and noted removing the persona made the task trivial. Our persuasive-persona seeding needs a defence prepared in advance.
(5) STATISTICS ON SMALL DIFFERENCES. Reviewers demanded standard errors across repetitions and actual significance tests where cross-model gaps were ~0.01. Consistent with our run-level clustering plan, but it must be visible.
(6) ECOLOGICAL VALIDITY OF SYNTHETIC INJECTION. Injected falsehoods were repeatedly called engineered and unmapped to real deployments, and binary/MCQ tasks were said not to transfer to open-ended settings.

ONE ENCOURAGING SIGNAL, reported because it cuts in our favour and should not be over-read: in TWO independent threads (MANBENCH yIoMqDes7O and DEBATE rMnZbCOhSS) reviewers spontaneously asked the authors to run MULTIPLE DIFFERENT LLMs within a single simulation, one explicitly reasoning that this better matches human societies where parties hold different knowledge. Reviewers are asking for our experiment. That is motivation evidence, not novelty proof.

UNRESOLVED ITEM REQUIRING A HUMAN: whether N4Cq7phkDY ("Misinformation Propagation in Benign Multi-Agent Systems", ACL ARR 2026 August) is the same work as the already-known arXiv:2606.16710 (Becker). ACL ARR is double-blind so authors are hidden and I could not settle it. This matters a great deal, because if it is a NEW group then threat axis 1 is independently occupied by a paper reporting same-family homophily in falsehood persistence. Resolve before the next literature pass.

Within OpenReview I did not exhaustively enumerate ICLR 2026 — 976 reviews surfaced from 49 relevance-ranked query-pages, but the venue holds far more, and a keyword-based scan will miss papers that use different vocabulary for the same constructs (e.g. "herding", "informational cascade", "groupthink" were not run as separate queries). findings.title: When Truth Is Distributed: Misinformation Derails Collective Fact Recovery in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
findings.authors: Chenfei Yan, Zeyang Yue, Feifei Zhao, Erliang Lin, Lu Jia, Haibo Tong, Mingyang Lyu, Chengyi Sun, Yi Zeng
findings.why_relevant: THE ONLY FORWARD CITATION OF THE TARGET, and it is ICML-accepted, so it will be the reference reviewers reach for. It injects misinformation adversarially ('controlled deception by a key evidence holder') and traces belief over multiple stages (multi-stage voting, testimony adoption, evidence-root lineage propagation) across 120 five-agent environments with distributed partial observation. Headline effect is enormous: collective truth recovery falls 72.50% -> 14.17% under injected deception. What it does NOT do is our contribution: it evaluates '3 homogeneous LLM-based multi-agent systems' — each population is single-family, so architectural diversity is never manipulated; there is no isolated-accuracy matching across populations; and the analysis is condition-contrast, not time-to-event. Our D0-D4 ladder, capability matching, and capitulation hazard all survive. But this paper now owns the 'adversarial injection derails multi-round collective fact recovery' headline, so our framing must lead with diversity-as-manipulation rather than with the existence of the effect.

findings.title: Hallucination Cascade: Analyzing Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
findings.authors: not captured on the abstract page fetch
findings.why_relevant: Crosses model-family heterogeneity WITH multi-round cascade depth — two of our five threat axes at once. Explicitly tests three distinct families (GPT-5.3, DeepSeek-V3, LLaMA-3-70B-Instruct) and analyses cascade depth in 3-agent chains, reporting a quantified amplification factor of 0.644 (net attenuation) with normalized hallucination falling from 0.422 at the first agent while factual accuracy also declines 0.789 -> 0.769. That accuracy-decline-alongside-error-suppression result is a direct empirical precedent for our truth-acquisition-vs-capitulation distinction, i.e. it has already shown that 'suppresses falsehood' and 'transmits truth' come apart. Mitigating differences: errors are naturally occurring hallucinations, not an injected persuasive falsehood with an adversarial persona; chains are depth-3, not a 20-agent graph; and heterogeneity is reported descriptively rather than manipulated against a capability-matched homogeneous control.
